provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for autumn: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 雨岩 ame-iwa, then 刈跡 kari-ato, then 麻布 asa-nuno, then 秋夕 aki-yu. NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Every adjacent pair of layers is more than ΔE00 5 apart — the distance below which the product calls two items the same (FR-44) — because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one; gate 11 recomputes that under the current engine on every run, so no figure is typed here. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: An autumn morning: a cool rain-grey (雨岩) outermost, the straw of a harvested field (刈跡), a pale linen layer (麻布) where the dew catches, and the dark red of autumn dusk (秋夕) as the innermost edge. The name is the one mockup 10 prints for this row: not coined here and not a documented kasane name, but a seasonal image, adopted as ours because it describes these layers.
